title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 17
paragraphs: He carried on the war with the Milesians, having inherited it from his father. He would invade their territory and besiege Miletus in this fashion: whenever the crops were ripe in the fields, he marched his army into their country to the sound of pipes, harps, and flutes of both male and female tone. When he reached Milesian land, he did not tear down the farmhouses, burn them, or rip off their doors — he let them stand just as they were. But the trees and the crops on the land he destroyed, and then retreated the way he had come. Since the Milesians controlled the sea, it was useless for his army to lay siege. He spared the houses so that the Milesians would have places to live while they sowed and tilled their fields, and so that through their labor he would have something to destroy the next time he invaded.
